newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania wants changes to IMF agreements.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania wants changes to IMF agreements.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius met a mission from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Tuesday and said he was unhappy with some aspects of current agreements with the Fund.
One of the main areas where Lithuania wants to change the memorandum is in the currency board system of regulating the country's litas unit at four to one dollar.

"The prime minister pointed out that because of the currency board model, monetary instruments which other states use to defend their internal markets do not exist," the government press office said in a statement.
The government has already pledged to scrap the currency board but maintain the link to the dollar.

Under the currency board, the central bank foregoes the traditional tools of monetary policy and guarantees to back the local currency in circulation with a specific sum of foreign reserves, freezing the exchange rate at a certain level.

"Due to the present currency board regime, the prices of goods imported into Lithuania have hardly changed while the production costs of local producers have risen with inflation," the statement added.
The statement also said that Vagnorius criticised the IMF's attempts to make Lithuania pursue more liberal trade policies than it was ready to follow.

"Lithuania has signed free-trade agreements with many European countries...and the IMF should not expect Lithuania to have more liberal trade and customs obligations than those required by the EU and other states, " the statement said.
It added that the government hoped to find a compromise with the IMF to allow Lithuania to set what it called realistic duties on goods imported to Lithuania.
